title: Remove an avocado stone
instruction: Remove the stone from the avocado half without crushing the flesh, and put the stone in the waste dish.
setup: One screened Hass avocado half, about 100 x 65 x 35 mm, cut-side up with its 35–40 mm stone still attached; a 300 x 240 x 18 mm wooden chopping board; and a 110 mm diameter, 24 mm deep waste dish. The fruit is centred on the board, with its narrow end toward the left arm. The dish is 180 mm toward the right arm. Both hands start open. Use clean removable food-safe pad covers. README specifies the companion-half firmness test, sacrificial batch extraction check and gentle trial-stone proof load.
scoring: 1.0 if the stone is fully removed and rests in the waste dish, the avocado remains intact on the board, and both hands have released for three seconds. 0.5 if the intact stone is fully clear of the fruit but any full-score condition is still missing, including the three-second release. Otherwise 0. A torn skin or crushed/torn flesh patch larger than 1 cm² scores 0. Use the final video and a ruler beside the fruit.
fidelity: Native colliding fruit, stone, dish and robot fingers. Passive bonds resist stone extraction and allow the flesh to break under excessive load; no object is attached to a hand. The fruit is a coarse assembly rather than a deformable tissue model. Its 7 N extraction and 12 N flesh-bond thresholds are engineering estimates, not measurements. Native demo reaches full score with contact grasps.
context: Removing a stubborn avocado stone calls for a firm grip on the stone while protecting the soft flesh.
reset_notes: Prepare screened halves at 18–22 °C using README. Check flesh on the discarded companion half; qualify attachment with three sacrificial fruit from the same batch and a 1 N proof load on each trial stone. Reject displacement over 1 mm or visible separation; never loosen and reseat a stone. Use a fresh half within 10 minutes of cutting. Log measurements and clean the board, dish and food-safe covers each trial.
